headline: US strikes on Iran rattle oil markets as Google posts a cracking earnings beat — but MSFT faces its own big test next week.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped last night ahead of its earnings report due July 29. Markets are nervous — analysts expect a potential 6.7% swing either way on results. Nothing's broken with the long-term story, this is classic pre-earnings jitters.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet actually posted a stellar Q2 — 12th straight quarter of strong revenue growth and 950 million monthly Gemini users. The dip last night looks like broader NASDAQ weakness dragging it down, not anything company-specific. The result itself was a beat.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped slightly last night, likely caught in the general tech sell-off. The main news around the company is that Rockstar Games workers held their first union talks ahead of the GTA 6 launch — something to watch but no immediate impact on the stock.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bounced nicely today, up 1.93% — one of the best performers in the portfolio this session. Analyst commentary suggests the lithium market is showing early tightening signals, with Liontown's self-funded growth adding to optimism. Still well below your cost base, but today's move is encouraging.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged higher today, helped by a generally positive ASX session and some emerging market tailwinds. The AUD has been essentially flat so no currency drag.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped a touch today, reflecting last night's NASDAQ softness which hit tech and AI-linked stocks. Global X also recently expanded its Australian ETF lineup with 26 new funds on ASX, which is a positive for the brand but no direct impact on this holding.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS eased slightly today, mirroring last night's mild S&P 500 dip. JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon has been making bearish noises about the US bond market, which can weigh on sentiment for broad US market funds — but nothing that changes the long-term case for holding a total US market index.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today — barely moved. The diversified nature of this fund means it absorbs daily volatility well. Nothing to see here.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings beat — but stock dipped anyway
watch_today.detail: Google's Q2 was genuinely impressive — 12 consecutive quarters of strong revenue growth, 950 million monthly Gemini users, and a clear earnings beat. The overnight dip of 1.24% appears to be broader NASDAQ weakness, not a reaction to bad news. For a long-term holder, this result actually strengthens the case to sit tight. Hold.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings on July 29 — brace for volatility
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports earnings next Tuesday (July 29, US time). Analysts are pricing in a potential 6.7% swing in either way. It's already down 1.86% last night on pre-earnings nerves, and is sitting at an 11.9% loss overall in your portfolio. The long-term cloud and AI story is still intact — don't let a single earnings swing spook you into selling. Hold through it.

watch_today.title: PLS popped today — but still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 1.93% today — a welcome move, but your position is still down 37% overall. The lithium market is showing early tightening signals and some analysts are calling recovery. This is a long-term recovery play — sit tight and let it play out. Don't add unless you're prepared for more volatility.

watch_today.title: Oil surges 3.2% on US-Iran strikes — watch inflation impact
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped $2.80 to $89.63/barrel last night after the US carried out military strikes on Iran. Higher oil means higher petrol prices and broader inflation pressure — which makes an RBA rate hike more likely (traders are already pricing in a fourth hike). This is worth watching for its flow-on effects on your mortgage or cost of living, not just the portfolio.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike odds rising — fourth hike increasingly likely
watch_today.detail: Markets are now pricing in a strong chance of a fourth RBA rate rise, driven by surging fuel prices from the Iran conflict and a strong domestic jobs market. If you have a variable rate mortgage, it may be worth checking with your lender. Higher rates also tend to weigh on growth stocks short-term — another reason to stay calm and think long-term with your US tech holdings.

watch_today.title: GXAI still well below cost — long-term AI thesis intact
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF is down 16.3% overall and slipped another 0.5% today. The AI sector is real and growing — Google's Gemini user numbers prove that — but the ETF has been caught in broader tech volatility. For a long-term holder, this is a hold. The theme isn't broken, it's just taking time to play out.

world.summary: The biggest story today is the US launching military strikes on Iran, sending oil prices surging and rattling nerves across the Middle East and beyond. Europe is also navigating a complex trade dilemma with China, and questions about American democracy are making headlines.

stories.title: US carries out military strikes on Iran as conflict escalates
stories.why_it_matters: The US military has carried out strikes on Iran, dramatically escalating what was already a tense standoff. Iran had warned of an 'eye for an eye' response if the US followed through on Trump's threats to destroy Iranian infrastructure. The strikes sent oil prices jumping 3.2% to nearly $90 a barrel overnight — meaning higher petrol prices are coming at the bowser. Australia has already issued updated travel warnings for Middle East countries as the situation deteriorates.

stories.title: US surges military forces toward Middle East, giving Trump more options
stories.why_it_matters: The Wall Street Journal reports that the US has been surging additional military forces toward the Middle East, giving the Trump administration a wider range of military options against Iran. This suggests the conflict could escalate well beyond the initial strikes. For everyday Australians, the key risk is prolonged high oil prices — which feed into petrol costs, freight, and ultimately the price of most goods in the shops.

stories.title: Jordan caught in the crossfire as US-Iran conflict widens
stories.why_it_matters: Jordan, a key US ally that shares borders with Iraq and Syria, is now being dragged into the widening conflict between the US and Iran. Countries like Jordan that have tried to stay neutral are facing enormous pressure as fighting spreads and proxy groups become more active across the region. A broader regional war would have serious humanitarian and economic consequences well beyond Iran itself.

stories.title: Europe faces a China trade dilemma as geopolitics reshapes global commerce
stories.why_it_matters: Europe is wrestling with a serious dilemma: it wants to maintain free trade and economic ties with China, but US pressure and geopolitical tensions are making that harder. The EU relies heavily on China for manufacturing and export markets, but aligning too closely with Beijing risks straining relations with Washington. This tug-of-war is reshaping global supply chains — which matters for Australia, whose own economy is deeply tied to both China and the US.

stories.title: Australia issues new Middle East travel warnings amid escalating conflict
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian government has updated its travel advice for multiple Middle East countries in response to the escalating US-Iran conflict. If you or anyone you know has travel planned to the region — including Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Iraq, or the UAE — check smartraveller.gov.au before you go. The situation is moving fast and advice could change again quickly.

markets.summary: The ASX had a quiet positive day, up 0.18% to close at 8,839. Last night in the US, the NASDAQ slid 0.57% and the S&P 500 edged down 0.14% as tech stocks gave back some ground. The big mover was oil — up 3.22% to nearly $90/barrel on the US strikes on Iran. Gold pulled back 1%. The Aussie dollar was essentially flat at 70 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Mild positive session on the ASX today.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night — barely moved, slight softness across the board.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night — tech stocks gave back gains, dragging NASDAQ lower.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big jump last night on US military strikes against Iran. Petrol price rises likely to follow.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back despite geopolitical tension — unusual, but short-term noise.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar essentially flat at 70 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA is dominating domestic headlines today — a new survey reveals most Australians don't fully understand how interest rates work, while markets are increasingly convinced a fourth rate hike is on the way, driven by surging fuel prices from the Iran conflict and a strong jobs market.

stories.title: RBA finds most Australians don't understand how interest rates work
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA has published a new community survey showing that a large chunk of Australians don't have a solid grasp on how interest rates affect things like mortgage repayments, savings, and inflation. This matters because rate decisions have a massive impact on household budgets — if you don't understand the mechanics, it's harder to plan ahead. The RBA says it wants to improve financial literacy as part of its communication strategy.

stories.title: Markets now twice as likely to price in an RBA rate hike as Iran war pushes fuel costs higher
stories.why_it_matters: The odds of the RBA lifting interest rates have roughly doubled, according to financial market pricing. The main driver is the US-Iran conflict pushing oil prices sharply higher — costlier fuel feeds directly into inflation, which the RBA is tasked with keeping under control. If another hike lands, it means higher repayments for anyone on a variable rate home loan.

stories.title: Traders increasingly convinced a fourth RBA rate rise is coming after jobs surge
stories.why_it_matters: A stronger-than-expected Australian jobs report has added fuel to the rate hike fire. When more people are employed, they spend more, which can push prices up — giving the RBA another reason to raise rates to cool things down. The AFR reports that bond traders (the people who bet real money on these outcomes) are now firmly in the camp expecting a fourth consecutive hike. Watch for the next RBA meeting announcement for the actual call.

ai.summary: Google's Gemini is under pressure from Chinese rival Kimi and its own delayed flagship model, while AI regulation is a hot topic both in Australia and globally. Anthropic just dropped $40 million on an AI regulation group.

stories.title: China's Kimi AI closes in on ChatGPT and Anthropic — while Google's Gemini slips
stories.why_it_matters: Kimi, an AI assistant built by Chinese startup Moonshot AI, is rapidly closing the gap on OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude in global benchmarks — while Google's Gemini is losing ground. This is significant because it shows the AI race is genuinely global, not just a US contest. For investors holding Google stock, it's a reminder that Gemini needs to keep pace — and right now, it's under pressure.

stories.title: Google delays its top Gemini model again — clouding earnings outlook
stories.why_it_matters: Google has delayed the release of Gemini 3.5 Pro — its most powerful AI model, which was announced at Google I/O — for the second time. Lighter, less capable models have been released instead. This is a concern for Google investors because it suggests the company is struggling to deliver its flagship AI product on schedule, at a time when rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic are moving fast. It's one reason last night's earnings beat didn't send the stock higher.

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic are cheering on AI regulation in Australia — here's why
stories.why_it_matters: It might seem strange that the world's biggest AI companies are actively lobbying FOR regulation — but it makes strategic sense. Strict rules favour well-resourced companies that can afford compliance, and create barriers for smaller competitors. OpenAI and Anthropic backing Australian AI regulation is less about safety and more about locking in their market position. Australia is seen as a useful testing ground for regulation frameworks that could go global.

stories.title: Anthropic donates $40 million to AI regulation group
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic (makers of Claude) has pledged $40 million to an AI policy and regulation group. That's a serious chunk of money going into shaping how governments write the rules around AI. Combined with their lobbying in Australia, it's clear that the AI giants are working hard to influence the regulatory environment — which will ultimately determine who wins and who loses in this space over the next decade.

sport.summary: NRL Round 21 kicks off tonight with Eels vs Panthers at 7:50pm. The Knights and Roosters will honour the late halfback Todd Dureau in their Friday clash. AFL MRO sanctions and team news are also rolling in ahead of the weekend.

stories.title: Knights and Roosters to honour late halfback Todd Dureau on Friday night
stories.why_it_matters: Friday night's clash between the Newcastle Knights and Sydney Roosters (6pm, McDonald Jones Stadium) will be a tribute game for Todd Dureau, a beloved NRL halfback who passed away. Both clubs are expected to pay their respects before kick-off. It adds a significant emotional dimension to what is already a big Round 21 game.

stories.title: NRL Round 21: Everything you need to know — teams, tips, odds
stories.why_it_matters: Round 21 is a big one — tonight's Eels vs Panthers at CommBank Stadium (7:50pm) leads things off. The weekend also features Knights vs Roosters, Rabbitohs vs Storm, Cowboys vs Broncos, and the Gold Coast Titans away to the Dragons on Sunday at 2pm. Dolphins have the bye this week.

stories.title: PNG Chiefs NRL team tracker — every signing confirmed so far
stories.why_it_matters: The PNG Chiefs — the NRL's 18th team set to enter the competition — are continuing to build their roster. CODE Sports is tracking every confirmed signing as the franchise takes shape. It's an exciting development for the game's expansion into the Pacific, and one of the bigger structural stories in the NRL this year.

stories.title: AFL MRO hands out major sanctions to two clubs
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's Match Review Office has handed down major sanctions to two clubs this week — suspensions and/or fines that could affect team selections heading into the weekend. Full details of which players are affected weren't available from the headline alone, but check AFL.com.au for the updated team lists before locking in your tips.

stories.title: AFL team whispers: Big Saint unlikely to return, McKay update, star Hawks back
stories.why_it_matters: AFL team whispers are in for the weekend: a prominent St Kilda player is 'unlikely' to return from injury, Ben McKay's availability is being monitored, and a key Hawthorn Hawks player is set to come back into the side. Specific names and injuries weren't fully confirmed from the available details — head to AFL.com.au for the full team lists before the selection deadline.
